countries/Austria: "is officially neutral and stays outside any military alliance" - constitutionally neutral and not in NATO, but EU membership carries a mutual-assistance clause; a reader may see that as alliance-like
countries/Brazil: "shares a vast system of waterfalls with a southern neighbour" - the Iguazu Falls are shared with a neighbour lying to the south-west rather than due south
countries/Denmark: "shares its only mainland border with a larger southern neighbour" - worded 'mainland' because since 2022 the realm also has a short land border on a small Arctic island with a North American state
countries/Germany: "had its capital divided by a guarded wall until 1989" - true of the present capital; during division the western state's capital was elsewhere
countries/Greece: "has thousands of islands scattered across warm, clear seas" - the count of several thousand includes islets; only about two hundred are inhabited
countries/Iraq: "was home to ancient civilisations where writing on clay tablets began" - cuneiform is usually dated as the earliest writing, but early hieroglyphic writing elsewhere is close in date
"has long been among the world's leading growers of date palms" - historically the top producer; its current rank among producers is lower and varies year to year
countries/Jamaica: "has long been a major producer of bauxite and alumina" - historically among the largest producers; its current world rank is lower (roughly top ten)
countries/Nepal: "abolished its monarchy and became a federal republic in 2008" - the monarchy was abolished and a federal democratic republic declared in 2008; the federal provinces were set up under the 2015 constitution
countries/Nigeria: "is home to a historic kingdom famed for cast brass plaques" - the famous plaques are mostly brass though commonly called bronzes; the kingdom shares its name with a neighbouring state (not named in the clause)
countries/Poland: "vanished from the map for over a century after being partitioned" - 1795 to 1918; dependent entities such as the Napoleonic duchy and the congress kingdom existed in between
"has a northeastern lake district with thousands of lakes" - the usual figure is about two thousand lakes
countries/Norway: "has twice rejected joining the European bloc in referendums" - the 1972 vote concerned the European Community and the 1994 vote the European Union, hence 'bloc'
